label: Raon-OpenTTS-1B local reference-conditioned speech adapter
summary: Use the official Raon-OpenTTS-1B checkpoint locally to make short English speech cues in an explicitly consented reference voice; it is speech-first, not a singing synthesizer, and the model card is CC-BY-NC-4.0.

handoffs.label: Generate bounded speech cues from a consented reference voice
handoffs.intent: Use one owned or explicitly consented reference recording to create short speech cues that can be arranged as an authored vocal texture or passed through a separate, declared pitch treatment.
inputs: An owned or explicitly consented reference WAV and the exact words spoken in it
An explicit consent/rights note for reference-voice cloning and intended use
A pinned Raon-OpenTTS model revision, checkpoint, config, vocoder, seed, and output role
Short cue text; Raon-OpenTTS is speech-first and does not accept this handoff as singing synthesis
For pitch treatment: an explicit musical intent, key, scale, preset, and separate raw-output path
outputs: New 16 kHz lossless WAV speech cues outside recordings/raw and FINAL
A manifest with reference checksum/transcript/consent note, model/checkpoint/config/vocoder identity, license, seed, settings, and output checksums
When tuning is requested, preserved raw cues plus per-cue EPRS autotune sidecars
steps: Create or activate the isolated `.eprs-local/raon-opentts-env` environment, clone the official KRAFTON checkout under `.eprs-local/raon-opentts`, install its dependencies, and obtain the 1B checkpoint plus 16 kHz HiFi-GAN vocoder without adding paths or credentials to public artifacts.
Verify the exact model revision and CC-BY-NC-4.0 terms; keep the reference audio local and do not send it to Hugging Face or another service.
Run `scripts/raon_opentts_voice.py` with the reference audio, exact reference transcript, required consent note, short cues, and a new song-local output directory.
If a cue needs musical pitch, prefer an authored target-note path or use `eprs autotune` only as a declared, reversible treatment; do not claim that speech TTS invented a sung melody.
Compare raw and processed cues in the complete arrangement, then promote only a listened candidate through the normal EPRS experiment and release gates.
verification: Confirm the reference checksum, transcript, consent note, model revision, checkpoint/config/vocoder checksums, seed, settings, and CC-BY-NC-4.0 license are recorded without embedding the reference audio.
Confirm every generated cue is a non-empty 16 kHz PCM WAV, opens cleanly, is not clipped or truncated, and has a matching output checksum.
For tuning, confirm voiced-frame coverage and target notes, then compare raw and tuned cues at matched level in stereo and mono.
Confirm the result is disclosed as a consented synthetic/reference-conditioned speech cue and is not presented as a human recording, singing model, creative approval, or release clearance.

preserve: The immutable reference recording, exact transcript, consent/rights note, model revision, checkpoint/config/vocoder identity, seeds, generated raw cues, processed alternatives, and checksums
The distinction between a consented reference-conditioned synthetic speech cue, an actual human vocal performance, and a musical pitch-treatment experiment
avoid: Uploading a private reference voice, cloning or imitating anyone without explicit consent, using the model for a child or identifiable third party without permission, or hiding model/license details
Treating the CC-BY-NC-4.0 model license as clearance for a reference speaker, generated output, commercial release, or platform upload
Calling speech-first TTS singing synthesis or using autotune as a substitute for authored melody
